title: Equipment Brokerage — Practitioner Testimony Operator Workbook
subtitle: A field workbook for consignment brokering, used-equipment price reading, auction bidding discipline, undercarriage and fluid inspection, lien clearance, payment fraud screening, and equipment finance referrals

worksheets.title: Brokerage Business Blueprint and Price-Reading Ledger
worksheets.purpose: Turn the consignment brokerage model into a working plan covering commission bands, three revenue lines, client-book sizing, seller screening, listing standards, negotiation scripts, and supply-driven price reading, so every unit you take on is priced on condition and tracked to a real net result instead of a hopeful gross spread.
instructions: Complete the commission and revenue-line fields first, because every later pricing decision depends on knowing what each consigned unit actually pays you.
Call at least three current or prospective sellers and use their answers to fill the seller story and days-on-market fields with real cases.
Pull recent auction results and dealer-lot listing counts for one model you plan to broker before writing the supply signal entry.
Inspect one older unit in person, counting hour-meter digits and checking housing tops for oil, before filling the condition and paperwork field.
Fill the net flip ledger with actual numbers from a past or pending deal, listing every overhead line rather than estimating from the gross spread.

fields.name: commission_model
fields.prompt: Define the fee structure for your consignment brokerage. State the commission percentage band you will charge, how it scales with unit value, and why you will never take ownership of the iron you list for a consigning seller.
fields.example: Charging 5% to 12% of unit value, kept whole with no split; a $250,000 unit at 5% pays $12,500 [Equipment Broker Academy — _c4_PRT-_rE @ 00:00:42]. The operation runs from a home office and truck, never owns a machine, and is built to close remotely, targeting over 50 percent of units sold sight unseen [Equipment Broker Academy — _c4_PRT-_rE @ 00:03:16].

fields.name: three_revenue_lines
fields.prompt: Map the three revenue streams you can earn from a single consigning seller. For each line, retail, wholesale, and auction, write the per-unit commission range you expect and the type of machine you would route through it.
fields.example: Retail a dozer or excavator for $2,700 to $4,500 per sale, wholesale units at $1,800 to $3,000, and send leftovers to auction at $1,200 to $2,000 per unit [Equipment Broker Academy — C4UjO7bAqGI @ 00:03:08]. Avoid the biggest mistake of earning from only one source when three exist from the same client [Equipment Broker Academy — C4UjO7bAqGI @ 00:01:16].

fields.name: client_book_sizing
fields.prompt: Calculate how many consigning clients you need to reach your first one hundred listed units. Use an average units-per-client figure, note what share of clients relist all year, and write the monthly prospecting target that follows.
fields.example: At 3.5 units per client, the first 100 units equals about 27 clients, and over a third of those clients relist equipment all year [Equipment Broker Academy — C4UjO7bAqGI @ 00:10:39]. Target: sign roughly three new consignors a month for nine months, then lean on the relisting third for repeat inventory instead of cold prospecting every unit.

fields.name: seller_story_call
fields.prompt: Script the first phone call you make to every seller before any money moves. List the questions that uncover why the machine is on the market, and note how you will screen tire kickers away from the seller.
fields.example: Opening question: why is it for sale, a fire, worn-out iron, or a job that ran out [Swarfcast — NZVF_mbrYPQ @ 00:07:21]? Only call the owner back when a serious buyer surfaces, the way a Boom & Bucket rep simply asked 'will you take the list price' [Boom & Bucket — wIrb4GAXyy0 @ 00:01:17].

fields.name: listing_presentation_standard
fields.prompt: Write the minimum presentation standard every listing must meet before it goes live. Specify photo count and angles, description depth, and the distribution channels you will push each listing to so it reaches the widest pool of qualified buyers.
fields.example: No listing goes live with poor photos or a thin description, because weak presentation cuts leads, offers, and final price [Pav Jam — 4aHgTjO_vNI @ 00:02:17]. Minimum: twenty sharp photos covering all four sides, cab, engine bay, and undercarriage, plus hours and serial in the text. Each approved listing then gets pushed to several channels at once through dealer software.

fields.name: phone_negotiation_script
fields.prompt: Draft the phone negotiation script you will use when buying or wholesaling a unit. Include your opening price probe, how you will exploit weak listings, and what you will do when the buyer wants something other than the listed machine.
fields.example: Probe with 'would it be crazy' to test a lower number by phone, and hunt badly presented listings because weak descriptions open tougher negotiation [Pav Jam — 4aHgTjO_vNI @ 00:02:55]. When an Idaho buyer passed on the listed machine, Graff got a discount on a 32mm unit from a California dealer and closed in a week [Swarfcast — NZVF_mbrYPQ @ 00:12:49].

fields.name: days_on_market_plan
fields.prompt: Set realistic days-on-market expectations for each seller before signing the consignment. Record a benchmark wait time, the condition-based price you will recommend, and the point at which you will revisit price instead of letting the unit go stale.
fields.example: Benchmark: the average 972M wheel loader waits 105 days before purchase, so sellers must play the long game [Mike Whicita- Where To Sell My Used Equipment — h_gTFo7GYEo @ 00:00:35]. Price on condition, not seller hope, because overpriced units die [Equipment Broker Academy — R8KSspUuldY @ 00:02:25]. Revisit price at day 105 if inquiries have stalled.

fields.name: supply_signal_read
fields.prompt: Before quoting any seller a price, record the supply signals shaping that model's market. Note dealer-lot listing volume, auction counts versus late-model units sold, and whether supply is tightening or spiking, then state which direction prices should move.
fields.example: Through May 7, 2026, machinery auctions ran up 19.5% while 1-3 year old units sold fell 19.9% [Farm Journal — t7mTa6TooFk @ 00:01:29]. Contrast: an S780 combine slid 8.4%, from $346,900 to $317,789, when dealer-lot supply spiked [Machinery Pete — 8dTCmixzqP0 @ 00:00:54]. Read: scarce late-model iron holds; oversupplied models soften.

fields.name: condition_and_paperwork_check
fields.prompt: List the lot-side condition checks and paperwork you will demand before pricing an older tractor or consigned unit. Include hour-meter verification, hidden-leak inspection points, and the service records that let you justify a documented-history premium to buyers.
fields.example: Count hour-meter digits: a 4430 showing 3,400 hours gets priced as a 13,000-hour tractor [PatrickShivers — vxI956OLj9E @ 00:14:24]. If the sides are spotless, climb up and check transmission and hydraulic housing tops for oil [PatrickShivers — vxI956OLj9E @ 00:04:57]. Collect work orders and warranty status, since documented history adds value [Machinery Pete — 3oDXLUOs8DU @ 00:06:28].

fields.name: net_flip_ledger
fields.prompt: Build the net profit ledger you will apply to every flip or brokered deal. List each overhead line beyond the gross spread, including labor, workshop, tools, consumables, and part-hunting time, and state the minimum net figure that justifies taking the deal.
fields.example: A UK flipper's 41-machine year showed gross profit eaten by overhead, so each flip is tracked net of wages, workshop, tools, oil, consumables, and part-hunting time [Find it Fix it Farm it — 8CoH6zx1FWE @ 00:16:51]. Ledger columns: purchase, sale, gross spread, then every overhead line. Any deal netting under the set floor after those deductions gets passed.

worksheets.completion_gate: Worksheet 1 is complete when every field holds a real figure or script, at least one seller call has been logged with the reason for sale, and one unit has been priced on condition with a net ledger showing positive profit after every overhead line.

worksheets.title: Auction Bidding Discipline and Undercarriage-Fluid Inspection Log
worksheets.purpose: Build a repeatable auction discipline and a measured inspection log for tracked machines, covering platform terms, landed cost, comps and hard stops, shortlist bidding, identity checks, pickup logistics, consignment expectations, undercarriage scoring, cover-up detection, and oil sampling, so no money moves on a machine you have not priced and proven.
instructions: Choose one live or upcoming auction lot and use it as the working case for every field on this sheet.
Read the full platform terms and call the auction house about pickup and payment before writing the terms and logistics entries.
Calculate landed cost and lock the hard stop in writing before the closing clock starts, never during the final minutes of bidding.
Measure undercarriage components against the wear chart yourself or with a technician, and never accept a seller's percentage off the top of their head.
Pull an oil sample on a warm machine, confirm how long the oil has been in service, and log lab results when they return.

fields.name: auction_platform_terms
fields.prompt: Before registering on any auction platform, summarize its terms. Record whether the sale is unreserved, how the closing clock extends with late bids, the payment methods accepted, and any insurance or pickup rules that could block you from collecting the machine.
fields.example: IronPlanet: active bidding extends the close, but no bids for the final 2 minutes ends it [IronPlanet — qHDv4e8rQQw @ 00:03:03]. Pickup terms demanding $1M of insurance were waived for self-pickup when called in advance at every house [Make Everything — x7M1QNicFvc @ 00:07:22]. Payment: wire preferred, with card surcharges of 3-4% noted.

fields.name: landed_cost_worksheet
fields.prompt: Write out the full landed cost for your target lot before you set any maximum bid. Include the hammer subtotal, buyer's premium or auction fee, sales tax, title fee, card surcharge, and transport, then compare the total against your resale value.
fields.example: Line items: subtotal, 10% auction fee, 13% HST, the $115 title fee, and about 3% card surcharge [613 Equipment Rentals — edx6wEhgoE8 @ 00:03:01]. Premiums elsewhere run 12-19%; at 15%, a $1,000 win adds $150 before state tax [Make Everything — x7M1QNicFvc @ 00:01:05]. Max bid equals resale value minus every line above.

fields.name: comp_set_and_hard_stop
fields.prompt: Record at least three recent auction comparables for the unit you plan to bid on, then set a hard stop price. Explain how you will lock that ceiling before the final minutes, when most bids land and every new bid extends the clock.
fields.example: Comps for a 2023 Cascadia: $85k, $82k, and $81k; the 572,000 km unit landed at $76,000 [ET Transport — wzN9KKrhTBo @ 00:43:07]. Hard stop locked before the last 3-4 minutes, when most bids land and each adds a 2-minute extension [ET Transport — wzN9KKrhTBo @ 00:18:36]. Ceiling written down: $80,000, no exceptions.

fields.name: multi_target_shortlist
fields.prompt: List several acceptable units instead of fixating on one favorite. For each, write the key spec such as hours or kilometers, your ceiling, and the condition that would make you drop it and move to the next target on the list.
fields.example: Shortlist of four trucks: the favored 361k-km unit ran to $102k and was abandoned, while a 572k-km unit went for $76k [ET Transport — wzN9KKrhTBo @ 00:35:55]. Rule: when any target passes its ceiling, switch immediately, because bidders who don't know when or where to stop overpay [ET Transport — PHnFlcmti2s @ 00:15:55].

fields.name: identity_and_function_risk
fields.prompt: Document how you will verify a lot's true identity and functional condition when no auction guarantees the machine works. Note serial or model plate checks, how you treat a running-video claim, and the repair budget you reserve for non-runners.
fields.example: Trust the serial plate, not the title; listers mislabel similar mills as Bridgeports, and an email to SawStop confirmed no warranty claims on a serial [Make Everything — x7M1QNicFvc @ 00:04:48]. A machine shown running in the listing stays unverified, so budget for water-in-oil and blow-by repairs [Diesel Down Under — cNP1VdOt1J4 @ 00:19:13].

fields.name: payment_and_pickup_logistics
fields.prompt: Plan the payment and pickup sequence after you win a lot. Record how you will wire funds and speed release papers, how you will confirm the pickup window, and the yard hours that could strand your truck and driver.
fields.example: Email the wire confirmation with the bidder number in the subject line to speed release papers; Graham's card on file was never charged [613 Equipment Rentals — edx6wEhgoE8 @ 00:09:55]. Confirm the pickup appointment window by phone rather than email before driving out, noting the yard closes at 4 [Makers Acres — vUTKwba3CBk @ 00:01:30].

fields.name: consignment_expectation_gap
fields.prompt: If you consign units into an auction for a seller, write the expected total next to a realistic estimate. Note the evaluation conversation you will hold with the auction house and how you will brief the seller about a soft market.
fields.example: A fleet of Cascadias, Volvos, and vans expected $250,250 in a Ritchie unreserved sale and realized $232,000 in what the seller called a tanking market [ET Transport — UnNSCtlW-0k @ 00:22:56]. AuctionTime runs an evaluation process to test whether expectations are realistic against its estimate [AuctionTime — JxE8MNAqxhQ @ 00:01:12]. Brief sellers on that gap upfront.

fields.name: undercarriage_measurement
fields.prompt: Record a component-by-component undercarriage measurement for any tracked machine you price. List link height, bushings, pitch, grousers, idlers, rollers, and sprockets against the wear chart, then total the score and state the worn percentage you will price from.
fields.example: A 2010 Komatsu with about 4,700 hours summed 1,010 of 3,200 points, 31 percent worn and 69 percent remaining [C&C Equipment — Hif9qgd9EEI @ 00:11:05]. Anything measuring 40 to 50 percent gets priced as needing undercarriage soon [C&C Equipment — Hif9qgd9EEI @ 00:11:54]. Replacement runs 12,000 to upwards of 70 grand [Volvo Construction Equipment – North America — L3kAdkTSgI4 @ 00:00:01].

fields.name: track_coverup_check
fields.prompt: List the walkaround checks you will run to catch undercarriage cover-ups before bidding. Include idler position, rail rocking, chain link count against OEM spec, sag measurement, track adjuster grease test, and the feel of the bushing tops.
fields.example: Check how far the front idler is pushed out and rock the rails, because tracks pumped up tight can hide worn links [C&C Equipment — Hif9qgd9EEI @ 00:02:25]. A piano-string chain can mean a cut link, so count links and grease-test the adjuster [Volvo Construction Equipment – North America — L3kAdkTSgI4 @ 00:07:20]. Feel bushing tops for flat spots.

fields.name: oil_sample_protocol
fields.prompt: Write the oil sampling protocol you will require before buying any used machine. Specify warm-up time, labeling, how you will confirm the oil's age, lab turnaround, sample cost, and the sampling interval you will keep after purchase.
fields.example: Run the machine about 20 minutes so fluid is homogenized [Carter Machinery — R9dHZ4P7yp0 @ 00:01:08]. Confirm oil age first, because a just-changed fill leaves nothing to measure [MEVAS The Heavy Equipment Inspectors — enf_Ct89j8o @ 00:02:03]. Engine samples cost under 10 dollars with 24 to 48 hour turnaround [EquipmentWorld — QYimn88ydQI @ 00:05:07]. Resample every 250 hours.

worksheets.completion_gate: Worksheet 2 is complete when a target lot has a written landed cost, three comps, a locked hard stop, a backup shortlist, a measured undercarriage score with cover-up checks logged, and an oil sample submitted or on file.

worksheets.title: Lien Clearance, Fraud Screening, and Finance Referral Desk
worksheets.purpose: Prove every machine is free of liens and every payment is real, then stand up a finance referral desk that sources deals through vendors, CPAs, and bankers, qualifies lenders by phone, collects performance deposits, and projects realistic commissions per funded deal instead of chasing the largest spread anyone has claimed.
instructions: Run the debtor-name UCC search and the separate secured-party search on a real pending deal before completing the lien fields.
Order plain copies where a results screen hides the collateral description, and keep search fees and copy payments separate as each state requires.
Post your payment fraud rules where every person handling a sale can see them, and rehearse the call-back verification step before the next closing.
Sign at least one referral partner to a one-page agreement before logging any finance deal on this sheet.
Phone-qualify a minimum of three lenders on bullet points and record their credit floors, ceilings, and asset preferences in the matrix.

fields.name: ucc_name_search
fields.prompt: Run and record the UCC search on the debtor's exact legal name before any deal proceeds. Note the state used, spelling and ampersand variations checked, filing dates against the five-year active life, and the collateral description pulled for each hit.
fields.example: Searched the exact legal name, because a misspelling or missing middle initial can hide a million-dollar lien [Garden Shop Pro — F-yeb_XOivY @ 00:05:32]. Ran both 'and' and ampersand versions after one secured party lost a large claim over that difference [CSC — mwPfMMgcYNI @ 00:05:24]. Ordered the $15 Texas plain copy to read collateral [Garden Shop Pro — F-yeb_XOivY @ 00:03:59].

fields.name: secured_party_and_county_search
fields.prompt: Record the second-pass searches that catch liens a debtor-name search misses. Note the separate secured-party name search, county land-record searches for bolted-down fixtures, and any prothonotary or other state-specific records the deal's location requires you to check.
fields.example: Ran a completely separate search under the secured party's name to surface blanket liens missed on the first pass [Garden Shop Pro — F-yeb_XOivY @ 00:03:29]. Also checked land records and prothonotary records, since some filings exist only in Secretary of State records depending on the state [Private Investigator Videos — 8OP-aPYhHHM @ 00:01:56].

fields.name: lien_payout_clearance
fields.prompt: Describe how you will clear any existing lien at closing so the buyer cannot lose the machine to the original lender. Note the payout split, who sends funds to the lender, and the proof that the underlying debt is satisfied.
fields.example: On a $10,000 sale, the dealer pays $8,000 directly to the finance company and $2,000 to the seller, guaranteeing removal of the encumbrance [OnWaterTVAustralia — VQXQTmAfjjo @ 00:08:30]. A UCC-3 termination alone never clears collateral; confirm the debt is actually satisfied before releasing the machine [Garden Shop Pro — xe1J4TAACZE @ 00:06:28].

fields.name: identifier_verification
fields.prompt: Record every identifier you match on the physical unit before accepting it into inventory. List serial number, HIN, VIN, or model plate location, how each matches the paperwork, and the question you ask when an identifier is missing or unreadable.
fields.example: Hull, motor, and trailer each checked for a readable HIN, serial, or VIN. When a trailer carried no identifiers, the question was why, and a weak answer meant walking away because it could be stolen product [OnWaterTVAustralia — VQXQTmAfjjo @ 00:12:46]. Every number matched against title and bill of sale before the unit entered inventory or listing photos.

fields.name: payment_fraud_screen
fields.prompt: Set your payment fraud rules for every sale. State which payment forms you refuse, how you handle third-party pickups by out-of-state buyers, and the exact verification steps you take whenever wiring instructions arrive or appear to change.
fields.example: No machine leaves on a cashier's check, and an out-of-state buyer sending an uncle or friend to collect is an automatic stop [Boom & Bucket — 6UVHinO3tHg @ 00:00:43]. Changed wiring instructions get verified only by calling a number already on file [Living in Fort Myers — sF15mNe2_l4 @ 00:01:34]. Lookalike domains and Google Voice numbers flagged TNR Holding [jesseleblancatlanta — aLJ1Y8lZsRs @ 00:07:39].

fields.name: finance_referral_sources
fields.prompt: List the referral partners who already hold a trusting equipment buyer. Name vendor reps, CPAs, and bankers by category, the niche you will focus on, and the public sources you will mine to find contractors who need financing now.
fields.example: Built entirely on relationships with equipment sellers already moving trucks and medical devices [Jermane Cheathem — 6laX1_643JA @ 00:00:16]. Niche: heavy construction. Weekly task: mine public municipal contract awards and infrastructure bids for regional contractors that just won major projects and need vocational fleets [Equipment Finance Academy — uzLIopNJDJY @ 00:04:17]. Vendor reps trained to quote monthly payments.

fields.name: referral_agreement_terms
fields.prompt: Draft the one-page written referral agreement you will sign with every partner before the first deal crosses. State who gets paid, how much, and when, plus how vendor reps will present your monthly payment quote to their buyers.
fields.example: One page per partner stating who gets paid, how much, and when, signed before the first deal crosses [Equipment Finance Academy — YIQEV-r00oA @ 00:04:02]. Vendor reps quote a monthly payment on every deal, ideally this company's payment, so the borrower sees those numbers first [BizLoanConsultants.com — kOdpTliR_HM @ 00:05:25]. Example anchor: $25,000 over five years is about $500 monthly.

fields.name: deal_intake_and_deposit
fields.prompt: Define the intake sequence for every finance file. Note whether the client is buying equipment or borrowing against existing equipment, the document package required by deal size, and when the signed proposal and performance deposit must arrive before submission.
fields.example: Credit app alone up to $75,000; above that, three years of tax returns or audited financials [BizLoanConsultants.com — kOdpTliR_HM @ 00:06:19]. Nothing goes to a lender until the proposal is signed and one monthly payment is posted as a performance deposit [BizLoanConsultants.com — kOdpTliR_HM @ 00:09:33]. Collateral deals on assets already carrying a UCC filing get killed.

fields.name: lender_pitch_matrix
fields.prompt: Build your lender pitch matrix. For each funding source, record the credit floor, application-only ceiling, soft-cost coverage, and asset types it prefers, and note how you will pitch by phone without revealing the company name too early.
fields.example: Lender A accepts a 580 score with no time-in-business minimum, varying by equipment type [Brennan Valeski — oP0hP2pgigg @ 00:05:19]. Lender B finances up to 125% of cost to cover delivery and installation [NerdWallet Small Business — yAx4SRG_bfs @ 00:00:55]. Every pitch goes by phone on bullet points, company name withheld until fit is confirmed [BizLoanConsultants.com — kOdpTliR_HM @ 00:14:56].

fields.name: commission_projection
fields.prompt: Project your realistic commission per funded deal. Compare the grounded per-deal range against higher spread claims, run the math on one target deal size in your niche, and note the timeline you expect from first contact to funding.
fields.example: Grounded baseline: a $4,200 first-deal commission on a $180,000 excavator, closed in 60 days [Equipment Finance Academy — p-1FbIYoOCs @ 00:00:00]. Upside case: a 4% to 5% spread on a $350,000 Caterpillar package pays $14,000 to $17,500 [Equipment Finance Academy — uzLIopNJDJY @ 00:01:24]. Planning figure: $4,000 per deal, 60-day cycle.

worksheets.completion_gate: Worksheet 3 is complete when one deal shows clean debtor and secured-party UCC searches, verified identifiers, written payment fraud rules, a signed referral agreement, three phone-qualified lenders in the matrix, and a commission projection grounded in a real deal size.

worksheets.title: Rental Utilization, Equipment Costing, and Heavy-Haul Quoting
worksheets.purpose: Convert every rental unit, owned machine, and oversize move into hard numbers so utilization bands, bare hourly costs, permit clocks, and escort charges are priced before a contract is signed or a load is booked.
instructions: Pull twelve months of rental contracts and calculate time utilization per unit before touching any rate, because the cost clock never stops ticking even on idle days.
Price every working day against all 365 days of the year and write the math out longhand so a partner can audit every assumption.
Separate bare ownership and operating cost from overhead and margin, and never bill a machine at its bare hourly figure.
Build each heavy-haul quote from the piece dimensions and weight, then hold the per-mile rate until the state-issued route and permit lead time are confirmed.
Review the completed sheet every Monday alongside the days-out check, and sell or reposition any unit that has sat idle for a full quarter.

fields.name: fleet_utilization_band
fields.prompt: Record the current time utilization for each rental unit, then place every machine inside the 40 percent breakeven, 60 percent healthy, or 70 percent-plus bands, noting which units sit below breakeven and what specific action will move them upward this quarter.
fields.example: Mini excavator 14 ran at 38 percent, under the 40 percent breakeven The Markup sets, while United Rentals targets 70 percent-plus [The Markup — 4ZnfP4pS7A8 @ 00:05:53]. Skid steer 3 sits at 62 percent, healthy. Plan: bundle the excavator with an attachment and delivery package rather than cutting the daily rate below current market.

fields.name: full_year_day_rate
fields.prompt: Write the daily rate for your highest-value unit, show the annual cost it must recover, and divide that cost across all 365 calendar days so the rented days carry the idle ones, not just the days you expect bookings.
fields.example: A Finance Insider says to price working days against all 365 days, since the industry runs only 50 to 65 percent annual utilization [A Finance Insider — pgvX9soJ0Kk @ 00:06:00]. Their model fleet of 12 units at $350 per day blended and 55 percent utilization booked about $500K against $550K in costs, a loss [A Finance Insider — pgvX9soJ0Kk @ 00:07:52].

fields.name: ancillary_revenue_stack
fields.prompt: List every fee you can attach to a rental beyond the base rate, including damage waivers, fuel markup, delivery, and attachments, then calculate how much each added line changes the monthly net on one representative machine in your fleet.
fields.example: Marginomics shows fees turning a $1,500 monthly rent net into $12,500, with waivers, fuel markup, delivery, and attachments carrying the profit the base rate cannot. My 30-ton excavator line: waiver added, fuel billed at markup, delivery both ways charged, attachment rented separately. Mr. Margins notes the business makes money when rental time outpaces depreciation [Mr. Margins — YzDJ7sPjIt0 @ 00:22:53].

fields.name: idle_quarter_review
fields.prompt: Run a Monday days-out check on every unit, flag any machine that has sat idle for a full quarter, and record whether you will sell it, reposition it, or bundle it, along with the date of that decision.
fields.example: Marginomics runs a Monday days-out check, sells any machine idle for a full quarter, and banks a $4K monthly wear reserve [Marginomics — Lx3Lqgr9q3w @ 00:07:04]. My compact track loader sat 94 days with no contract, so it goes to sale. Mr. Margins warns that price-slashing to reach 80 percent is a trap [Mr. Margins — YzDJ7sPjIt0 @ 00:13:21].

fields.name: owned_equipment_hourly_cost
fields.prompt: Break each owned machine into ownership cost per hour and operating cost per hour, add them for a bare hourly cost, then show the overhead and margin you will layer on before that figure ever reaches a customer bid.
fields.example: Build Like A Pro TV breaks a $65K skid loader into $11 per hour ownership plus $20 operating, a $31 bare cost that must never be billed at $31 [Build Like A Pro TV — KWBdujV7H9Q @ 00:08:02]. My mini excavator: $14 ownership, $22 operating, $36 bare. Overhead and margin get layered on before the hourly rate goes into any bid.

fields.name: truck_ownership_timecard
fields.prompt: Calculate the true monthly cost to own each work truck across its expected service life, subtract resale, strip out fuel, and describe how the truck and other equipment will appear on timecards so jobs carry them instead of overhead.
fields.example: George Hedley puts a contractor truck at about $1,800 a month plus gas, from a six-year total of $192K, roughly $180K after resale [George Hedley | HardHat BIZCOACH — 60uc8gnDCiY @ 00:04:05]. He puts equipment on timecards so bookkeepers stop burying it in overhead [George Hedley | HardHat BIZCOACH — 60uc8gnDCiY @ 00:05:48]. My crew truck now posts to job cost daily.

fields.name: heavy_haul_quote_build
fields.prompt: Build a heavy-haul quote from the piece itself by listing dimensions and weight, then pricing the truck rate, state permits, pilot cars, police escorts, power assistance, weekend curfews, and the deadhead leg before you commit any per-mile figure.
fields.example: Scott Woods bid a 250,000-lb, 125-ft CAT 777 from Phoenix to the Port of Seattle at $25 to $30 a mile over 1,600 miles, roughly a $50,000 move [Freight Profits — qHs0sXdzamw @ 00:14:07]. A Nevada weekend sit added about $1,000 in pilot car costs [Freight Profits — qHs0sXdzamw @ 00:10:40]. My dozer quote now prices curfews and deadhead.

fields.name: oversize_trigger_and_permit_clock
fields.prompt: Compare each load against the 75-foot length, 8-foot-6 width, 13-foot-6 height, and 80,000-pound triggers, then record which states require permits, the expected permit wait, and the route mileage confirmed on the state-issued permit rather than routing software.
fields.example: Trinity Logistics sets triggers at 75 feet, 8 feet 6 inches, 13 feet 6 inches, and 80,000 pounds, with permit fees from $15 to over $70 [Trinity Logistics — oQI9qiLLIwA @ 00:02:36]. Woods saw an 863-mile PC Miler run become 1,700 miles on permit [Freight Profits — qHs0sXdzamw @ 00:18:13]. I hold the rate until the state-issued route arrives.

fields.name: pilot_car_rate_card
fields.prompt: Enter the escort rate card you will bid with, separating chase car and pole car per-mile rates, overnight charges, no-go day charges, hotel costs, and minimum day rates for short moves, so no escort expense surprises the final invoice.
fields.example: Woods bids chase cars at $1.65 a mile, $85 overnight, $250 a day for a no-go plus hotel, and about $600 as a day rate under 300 miles; pole cars run $1.85 to $2.00 a mile [Freight Profits — qHs0sXdzamw @ 00:09:06]. One bidder skipped pilot cars and lost about five grand [Freight Profits — qHs0sXdzamw @ 00:02:49].

fields.name: fleet_maintenance_control
fields.prompt: Describe the work order system tracking your fleet, the share of annual work orders that are preventive versus breakdown, the trigger you use for preventive service, and the off-rent confirmation process that stops idle rented equipment from accruing charges.
fields.example: Yvette Aubin says 25 preventive orders out of 100 means 75 percent are breakdowns or major repairs [Beiing Human — sNcACw9iXI0 @ 00:13:15]. Only 20 percent of contractors run work order systems [Beiing Human — sNcACw9iXI0 @ 00:20:33]. We set service by engine hours and log every off-rent confirmation number separately from the crew's last day [The Profitable Contractor — jLx7fLatA3A @ 00:02:50].

worksheets.completion_gate: Worksheet 4 is complete when every fleet unit has a utilization band, a full-year day rate, and a bare hourly cost with markup shown, and every pending heavy-haul quote lists permits, pilot cars, police escorts, curfews, and the deadhead leg.

worksheets.title: Carrier Compliance, Broker Vetting, and CNC Purchase Economics
worksheets.purpose: Protect freight-dependent equipment deals from broker failure and status errors, and size any CNC machine purchase against real machine-hour profit, survival cash, and under-power proof before money moves.
instructions: Verify broker security by phone with the bond agency every time, because no alert arrives when a bond drains below the federal floor.
Log days to pay as a running trend for each broker, and set a written cutoff before any payment dispute arises.
Match the USDOT number on the physical truck to the paperwork at every pickup and record the result on the load file.
Model CNC revenue at low, middle, and high productive hours, then net each scenario against every operating cost before calling any figure profit.
Refuse to wire funds on any used machine not seen running under power, and anchor its identity to the physical nameplate serial.

fields.name: broker_security_verification
fields.prompt: Before hauling or brokering any load, record the broker's SAFER status, licensing and insurance portal result, BMC-84 or BMC-85 filing, and the bond agency's phone confirmation that the full $75,000 security is actually in place on the date checked.
fields.example: Trucking Made Successful pulls SAFER and the licensing and insurance portal, confirms the BMC-84 or BMC-85, then calls the bond agency [Trucking Made Successful — iwQkqbEBCrM @ 00:08:15]. From January 16, 2026, a broker under $75,000 has seven calendar days to replenish [Trucking Made Successful — iwQkqbEBCrM @ 00:01:54]. My log: bond agent confirmed by phone, initials recorded.

fields.name: days_to_pay_trend
fields.prompt: Chart each broker's days to pay across at least the last several loads as a trend line, note any factoring grade or credit score you can see, and state the threshold at which you stop accepting that broker's freight.
fields.example: Days to pay is tracked as a trend, because a broker whose number keeps climbing is showing cash-flow trouble [Trucking Made Successful — iwQkqbEBCrM @ 00:09:11]. One broker rated an F with RTS Factoring kept posting loads anyway [Trucking Made Successful — iwQkqbEBCrM @ 00:05:22]. My cutoff: three consecutive increases past 45 days ends new tenders.

fields.name: usdot_match_check
fields.prompt: When a load is tendered or a truck arrives, write the USDOT number painted on the actual truck, the number on the paperwork, and whether they match, plus the action taken whenever the two numbers or company names disagree.
fields.example: The funny farm reports YMC Transport trucks kept rolling under MLTZX Group after the shutdown order, so the rule is to check the USDOT number on the truck that shows up [the funny farm — t1CJB1XA9y0 @ 00:01:36]. Tuesday pickup: paperwork matched, door number did not, load held until the carrier explained in writing.

fields.name: self_lookup_and_status
fields.prompt: Look up your own company the way a broker would on the Company Snapshot and the public Motus search, then record your carrier type, required coverage number, any status errors, and the escalation path you will use if normal channels stall.
fields.example: Jim Campbell says to check carrier type and required coverage, then call your agent before changing anything in the system [Jim Campbell - Official Trucking Channel — misVtmF2XjA @ 00:07:17]. Darryl Gibbs's dead DOT number sat almost three months until an Overdrive inquiry fixed it in 16 hours 26 minutes [Jim Campbell - Official Trucking Channel — misVtmF2XjA @ 00:08:44].

fields.name: complaint_and_dvir_discipline
fields.prompt: Describe when you will file an FMCSA complaint, what facts on authority or name misrepresentation you will attach, how you separate complaints from unpaid invoice collection, and how drivers complete a physical walk-around before signing any electronic DVIR.
fields.example: Freight Pro Hub warns a low rate con alone is not a federal violation [Freight Pro Hub — 8X37vkZBHyo @ 00:01:16], and a complaint is not a collection tool [Freight Pro Hub — 8X37vkZBHyo @ 00:03:41]. Tapping all good from the cab is fraud that costs CDLs [Trucking Life with Shawn — UlW-GlLugUg @ 00:06:26]. Our drivers complete the walk-around before signing.

fields.name: cnc_machine_hour_model
fields.prompt: Model one CNC machine's yearly revenue at your local machine-hour rate across low, middle, and high productive-hour scenarios, then net each scenario against material, tools, coolant, operators, setup, rent, inspection, financing, and downtime to reach actual profit.
fields.example: Money Machines models one lathe at $80 per machine-hour: $96K, $128K, and $160K at 1,200, 1,600, and 2,000 productive hours, all labeled revenue rather than profit [Money Machines — Q00deIDcQRw @ 00:03:14]. Each figure is then netted against material, tools, coolant, operators, setup, rent, inspection, financing, and downtime [Money Machines — Q00deIDcQRw @ 00:04:15].

fields.name: new_vs_used_price
fields.prompt: Record the new price and the used market price for the specific CNC model you are considering, then explain which purchase leaves enough cash to survive slow months and how the price difference changes your machine-hour breakeven point.
fields.example: Money Machines prices a new Haas SD10, a 6,000 RPM, 15 hp, 12-station-turret lathe, at about $65,000 versus $27-30K used [Money Machines — Q00deIDcQRw @ 00:00:15]. A CNC lathe without orders is an expensive piece of industrial furniture [Money Machines — Q00deIDcQRw @ 00:05:08]. Buying used keeps roughly $35K liquid for the slow first year.

fields.name: six_month_payment_test
fields.prompt: Apply the six-month survival test by writing your monthly machine payment, multiplying it by six, and showing the cash or credit that would cover those payments if every customer disappeared tomorrow, plus your expected payment terms from customers.
fields.example: TITANS of CNC MACHINING says you should still make the machine payment for 6 months if you lost every customer [TITANS of CNC MACHINING — bqSGI0L8zm0 @ 00:16:50]. Customers on 30-to-90-day terms often pay 30-45 days late [TITANS of CNC MACHINING — bqSGI0L8zm0 @ 00:31:00]. A $288.55 monthly Tormach PCNC 440 payment needs $1,731.30 reserved.

fields.name: under_power_inspection
fields.prompt: For any used machine purchase, record whether you saw it running under power in person, by FaceTime video, or through a third-party technician, and note rigging quotes, markups questioned, and whether the seller kept the machine powered through the sale.
fields.example: Contend Capital says a FaceTime video or third-party tech gets you 90% there and can save a $2K trip, though an in-person visit is still recommended [Contend Capital — rLDoLaoEZ-A @ 00:03:33]. A repo machine worth $50K collapses once it goes dark [Contend Capital — rLDoLaoEZ-A @ 00:04:33]. Our VMC was watched cutting live before any wire.

fields.name: import_identity_and_tooling
fields.prompt: For imported or older used iron, record the physical nameplate serial, build date, and retrofit date separately from PO and packing references, then describe how you will control tooling inventory and reorder points once the machine lands on the floor.
fields.example: SARK Engineers & COnsultants keeps build and retrofit dates separate and anchors identity to the nameplate serial over PO and packing references [SARK Engineers & COnsultants — Qiyq7yhmD2o @ 00:02:57]. JLCCNC guards tens of thousands of dollars of tooling behind a facial-recognition vending machine [Strange Parts — YuSApjBn_zY @ 00:15:45]. Our mill's nameplate serial now anchors every record.

worksheets.completion_gate: Worksheet 5 is complete when every active broker has a verified bond confirmation and a days-to-pay trend, your own carrier status has been checked, and any CNC purchase passes the six-month payment test and an under-power inspection.

worksheets.title: Imaging, Data-Center Power, Salvage, and Adjacent Deal Models
worksheets.purpose: Prove the technical identity and condition of exiting imaging and power equipment, then screen salvage, surplus, auction, parts-out, and export opportunities so the brokerage owns the buyer network instead of carrying risky iron.
instructions: Collect identity paperwork first: nameplates, series tags, tube scan seconds, software licenses, battery date codes, and acceptance test reports.
Photograph test equipment and its calibration dates and attach them to the check sheet the same day so results cannot be questioned later.
Compare reconditioned and new pricing across the full ownership period, including post-warranty service, not just the purchase price.
Screen every salvage or surplus unit for demil code, fluid condition, wear, and burn damage before placing any bid.
Never ship heavy iron or extend a net guarantee without a verified purchase order or adequate reserves documented in writing.

fields.name: imaging_system_identity
fields.prompt: Before pricing any MRI or CT system, record year, make, model, tube age, scan seconds or milliamp seconds, configuration, licensed software, and a photo checklist covering the glamour shot, series tag, computers, and gantry front, back, and side.
fields.example: Block Imaging asks first for year, make and model, then actual usage, tube age, scan seconds, configuration, and licensed software [Block Imaging — 4suol4m0dq4 @ 00:01:19]. Anyone on staff can shoot the glamour shot, series tag, computers, and gantry from front, back, and side, which confirms age and configuration [Block Imaging — 4suol4m0dq4 @ 00:02:26]. Our CT file is complete.

fields.name: reconditioned_vs_new_cost
fields.prompt: Compare new, used, and reconditioned pricing for the imaging modality you are brokering, then build a multi-year cost of ownership showing purchase price gap, warranty term, and annual post-warranty service cost from both the OEM and the independent refurbisher.
fields.example: MXR Imaging puts reconditioned MRI and CT at 40 to 50% below new [MXR Imaging — Nw9qRw-Y6TE @ 00:06:53]. Its six-year MRI comparison ran OEM 805 versus MXR 595, plus service at $85,000 instead of $110,000 a year, for $335,000 saved [MXR Imaging — Nw9qRw-Y6TE @ 00:26:53]. Block Imaging says new can cost twice as much [Block Imaging — VOR_RnHfhE4 @ 00:00:46].

fields.name: refurbisher_vetting
fields.prompt: Document how you vetted the refurbisher behind a reconditioned imaging system, including a live video walk of its parts floor, ISO 13485 certification, coil signal to noise ratio sheets, warranty inventory backing, and the cradle-to-grave paper trail received.
fields.example: MXR Imaging says a phone video walk should show parts, magnet farms, chillers, and cold head subassemblies, and you should ask how much inventory actually backs your warranty [MXR Imaging — Nw9qRw-Y6TE @ 00:05:45]. Every coil should be system tested and ship with a signal to noise ratio sheet from an ISO 13485 certified company [MXR Imaging — Nw9qRw-Y6TE @ 00:30:28].

fields.name: site_readiness_and_condition
fields.prompt: Before a buyer commits to an imaging system, record the building and installation survey findings, any added construction work, and the internal condition check confirming the equipment is clean beneath the covers rather than cosmetically refreshed on the outside only.
fields.example: Reclaim Atlas pictures a clinic that found an attractive scanner without checking its building, then watched the installation survey reveal additional work [Reclaim Atlas — XEbn26lA8EE @ 00:05:21]. Brown's Medical Imaging says buyers of preconditioned equipment do not want beautiful covers hiding a dirty interior [Brown's Medical Imaging — DpGCQ1Ijs-Y @ 00:00:33]. Our buyer's survey happens before deposit.

fields.name: generator_ups_proof
fields.prompt: For any standby generator or UPS in a data-center exit, record nameplate, kilowatt or kVA rating, voltage, fuel type, operating hours, battery date codes, maintenance history, and the load bank test result proving it carries demand rather than idling.
fields.example: Reclaim Atlas pulls the nameplate, kilowatt rating, voltage, fuel type, operating hours, and maintenance history, then requires a load bank test so the generator proves it carries demand instead of merely starting and idling [Reclaim Atlas — jfdR4HzT3cU @ 00:02:49]. On the Oak Ridge job, generator and UPS resale covered removal and paid the owner $12,000 [Reclaim Atlas — jfdR4HzT3cU @ 00:00:13].

fields.name: powertrain_packaging_and_removal
fields.prompt: Decide whether each power asset sells as a complete powertrain or as separate pieces, then estimate removal costs including crane access, and record the design-day peak sizing checks a buyer will need for step loading, power factor, and UPS recharge.
fields.example: Reclaim Atlas sells a generator with its transfer switch and paralleling gear because pieces designed together are more attractive [Reclaim Atlas — jfdR4HzT3cU @ 00:07:41], but resale value can disappear when removal needs a crane [Reclaim Atlas — jfdR4HzT3cU @ 00:06:00]. Keentel Engineering rejects average PUE math and sizes for design-day peak [Keentel Engineering — nico3vxC_dA @ 00:17:52].

fields.name: salvage_and_surplus_screen
fields.prompt: For each flood-salvage or government-surplus unit under consideration, record the source, demil code, data plate match against the catalog, fluid condition, pin bosses, grouser height, burn damage, and the rebuild scope you expect to schedule for the slow season.
fields.example: Vantor Surplus says read the demil code first; DEMIL A and Q transfer intact while higher codes get torch-cut [Vantor Surplus — lExAdQTwxNk @ 00:12:24]. EquipmentWorld's contractor buys underwater units from insurers and salvagedsale.com but skips burned machines [EquipmentWorld — w3saQAgnyLI @ 00:01:46], and has put about 2,000 hours on one since submersion after a cheap rebuild.

fields.name: auction_house_fee_stack
fields.prompt: If you run or use an auction model, write the seller fee and buyer premium percentages, compute the house take on a representative machine, and state your policy on net guarantees, reserves, and keeping consignor proceeds off operating accounts.
fields.example: Plain Finance stacks a 6% seller fee and a 10% buyer premium for $3,200 on a $20K machine [Plain Finance — 9kP-CdkchRk @ 00:02:57]. A net guarantee without reserves turned $620K in comps into a $375K sale and a $150K hit [Plain Finance — 9kP-CdkchRk @ 00:06:18]. The sellers' proceeds never touch your account [Plain Finance — 9kP-CdkchRk @ 00:11:48].

fields.name: parts_out_economics
fields.prompt: For any whole unit you might part out instead of resell, list purchase price, tow, labor, other costs, and expected parts revenue, then compare the parted-out operating profit against selling the unit whole to the best available buyer.
fields.example: CapitalCode bought an F-150 for $1,500 and parted it out for $4,000; after a $150 tow, $600 labor, and $350 other costs, operating profit landed near $1,400 [CapitalCode — 5TO0VTTHS0w @ 00:01:54]. Garage Profits frames it plainly: you're not selling trash, you're selling raw material [Garage Profits — InQ7-NaPvxs @ 00:01:36]. Our donor unit beats whole-unit offers.

fields.name: export_buyer_verification
fields.prompt: For export or import machinery deals, record the buyer's verified purchase order, payment split, end-use screening, refused buyer categories, and the in-person dealer introductions you made to build the local buyer network that the brokerage, rather than the iron, will own.
fields.example: SwiftBridge Trading LLP locks a verified buyer and purchase order before shipping heavy iron, works 50/50 terms, and refuses galamsey buyers outright [SwiftBridge Trading LLP — XbLz7kvZIwc @ 00:05:16]. At Flying Wheels, Craig's in-person introductions to established local dealers produced location leads [Flying Wheels — en-0Xomp1UQ @ 00:11:56]. Our Ghana excavator ships only after PO verification.

worksheets.completion_gate: Worksheet 6 is complete when every imaging or power asset has full identity documentation and a proof test on file, and every adjacent deal shows fee math, salvage screening results, and a verified buyer before any commitment is made.
